title: Is Your Website Ready for Digital Marketing? A Pre-Campaign Check
description: Check whether a small-business website has a clear offer, relevant landing page, working enquiry route, usable mobile journey and meaningful measurement before a campaign.
summary: Follow a fictional Varanasi event-decor studio as it checks the destination, enquiry path and measurement before sending more visitors to its website.
body:
Is your website ready for digital marketing? Before sending more people to it, confirm five things: the offer is specific, the landing page matches the campaign promise, the next action works, the mobile experience supports that action, and the business can distinguish a completed enquiry from a page visit. If one of those foundations is missing, fix it before widening the campaign.

A campaign can create visits without creating useful conversations. The website is the place where a visitor checks relevance, understands the service and decides whether to act. Readiness therefore means that the destination can support one defined customer decision and that the business can verify what happened afterwards.

Kavya is ready to advertise before her website is ready to receive

Imagine Kavya runs a fictional event-decor studio in Varanasi. The business and situation are original planning examples, not a SiteSutra client story or reported result. She wants to promote wedding-stage design for the coming season and asks a digital marketing provider to start immediately.

Her homepage says only “We make every moment special.” It does not explain the service area, types of events, planning process or what a requester should prepare. The gallery mixes unrelated services. The enquiry button opens a form that has not been tested recently, and nobody has defined which submissions count as suitable project enquiries.

Kavya does not need a larger campaign plan yet. She needs a destination that can answer the visitor's first questions and a response path the business can operate. She turns campaign readiness into five evidence checks.

Separate campaign work from website repair

Kavya's hypothetical readiness review
QuestionEvidence to inspectIf it is missingOwner
Can a visitor recognise the exact offer?Service, audience, location and boundaries appear in plain languageClarify the offer before writing campaign messagesBusiness owner
Does the destination continue the promise?Headline, proof, details and next action match the campaign topicPrepare or revise the relevant landing pageContent and website owner
Can the visitor complete the next action?Form, WhatsApp, phone or booking route works from a real deviceRepair delivery, validation and confirmationWebsite and response owner
Does the page work on a small screen?Readable text, clear navigation, stable layout and usable controlsResolve the blocking mobile issuesWebsite owner
Can the business evaluate the outcome?A completed action and a qualified enquiry have separate definitionsAgree measurement and ownership before launchMarketing and sales owner

The review does not need a perfect website or a large redesign. It identifies the smallest missing condition that would make campaign evidence unreliable or the visitor journey unusable.

1. Make the offer specific enough to match

Kavya chooses one campaign offer: consultation for wedding-stage design in the Varanasi service area. The page explains the event type, what the consultation covers, what information the requester should prepare and which requests need a separate discussion.

This is more useful than a broad promise about “all event solutions.” A visitor who clicked a specific message should not have to search the whole site to discover whether that service exists. The business can still offer other services elsewhere; the campaign destination owns one clear decision.

2. Continue the campaign promise on the landing page

Google Ads describes a landing page as the page reached after an ad click and says landing-page experience includes usefulness and relevance, ease of navigation and whether the page meets the expectation created by the ad. Kavya therefore compares the campaign message with the destination line by line.

If the message offers wedding-stage consultation in Varanasi, the page should not lead with corporate conferences in another region. The headline, supporting explanation, project-fit information and next action should belong to the same promise. A dedicated page may help when the existing service page covers several different decisions, but a new URL is not automatically required.

Kavya also checks the final URL and domain with the campaign owner. Google Ads requires the landing-page domain and display URL domain to match. Account setup, policy review and campaign configuration remain separate from the content decision.

3. Test the next action as a customer would

The team chooses a short project form for structured requests and keeps WhatsApp for quick questions. Before any campaign begins, Kavya submits the form from a phone using a non-business email address. She confirms that required fields are understandable, the request reaches the monitored inbox, the page reports the real outcome and the assigned person can reply.

The test continues beyond the click. A button that opens the right screen but delivers nothing is not complete. The response owner, working hours and fallback belong in the readiness record.

Kavya also checks what happens when delivery fails, a required field is incomplete or the visitor uses a keyboard. These checks protect every source of traffic, not only paid campaigns.

4. Check the complete mobile task

Google Ads recommends a mobile experience with simple navigation, readable content and a clear way to take action. Kavya opens the real page on a small screen, dismisses no development shortcuts and completes the enquiry route.

She checks whether the headline is visible without awkward horizontal scrolling, buttons are distinguishable, labels remain attached to fields, the keyboard does not cover the current control and confirmation appears near the submitted action. She also checks that large media does not prevent the visitor from reaching the useful content.

A performance score can support investigation, but it cannot confirm that the offer makes sense or the notification arrives. Kavya records technical observations alongside the human task rather than treating one number as campaign readiness.

5. Define an action and a qualified outcome

Kavya separates three measurements: a landing-page visit, a successful form submission and a project enquiry accepted for a relevant next step. Google Analytics calls an action important to the business a key event and recommends events such as generate_lead for lead-generation measurement.

The website should record the successful action only after the intended completion point. A page view alone is not an enquiry. A form submission can still be spam, outside the service area or unrelated to the offer. Kavya keeps the qualified-enquiry decision in the business workflow and compares it with campaign activity later.

She does not place names, phone numbers, message contents or other unnecessary personal information in analytics events. Consent and privacy configuration must match the tools and jurisdictions actually used.

Fix blockers in sequence

  1. Offer: agree the service, intended audience and boundary.
  2. Destination: make the page continue that promise and answer the decision.
  3. Action: connect, test and assign the enquiry route.
  4. Mobile task: complete the journey on a real small screen.
  5. Measurement: verify the completed action and define qualification separately.

If the offer is unclear, changing button colour will not solve it. If delivery is broken, adding more analytics will not recover the missing request. The sequence keeps the team on the earliest unresolved dependency.

Run a local campaign-readiness check

Mark only conditions supported by current evidence. This tool runs in the page, stores nothing and does not estimate campaign performance, enquiries or rankings.

Can this destination support a controlled campaign test?

Complete the checks with the business, website and response owners.

No checks marked. Begin with the exact offer and visitor decision.

Document evidence instead of saying “the website looks fine”

Download the website campaign-readiness worksheet (CSV). Replace the hypothetical rows with the real offer, URL, device test, delivery result, owner and evidence link.

Give every unresolved row an owner and a review condition. “Fix before launch” is useful only when the team knows what completion looks like. Keep advertising budget, campaign management fees and website repair scope separate in the commercial agreement.

Launch only what the website can support

Kavya does not rebuild the whole website. She clarifies one offer, prepares the relevant destination, repairs and tests the enquiry route, completes the mobile task and defines how a suitable enquiry will be reviewed. The campaign team now has a controlled starting point instead of sending traffic to an untested general homepage.
